A [[small forward]], he was drafted in the [[2004 NBA draft]] by the [[Miami Heat]] directly out of high school. He also played for the [[Golden State Warriors]], [[Philadelphia 76ers]] and [[Portland Trail Blazers]]. He once led the league in three-pointers made, and was selected to participate in the NBA [[Three-Point Contest]] in 2011. ==High school career== Wright attended [[Washington Preparatory High School]] in ninth and tenth grade before transferring to [[Leuzinger High School]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/los-angeles/lakers/post/_/id/21257/the-l-a-in-my-game-with-dorell-wright|title = "The L.A. In My Game," with Dorell Wright|date = July 24, 2011}} After his senior year at Leuzinger, he enrolled as a [[super senior|fifth-year senior]] at [[South Kent School]] in [[Connecticut]], where he averaged 29.4 points, 14 rebounds and 5 blocks per game in basketball. Considered a five-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Wright was listed as the No. 4 small forward and the No. 12 player in the nation in 2004.{{cite web|url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/maple/21495|title=Dorell Wright Recruiting Profile|work=Rivals.com|access-date=January 3, 2006}} He initially committed to attend [[DePaul Blue Demons men's basketball|DePaul]] before entering the NBA draft.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/dorell_wright/bio/|title=Dorell Wright bio|work=NBA.com|access-date=April 13, 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140409222928/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/dorell_wright/bio/|archive-date=April 9, 2014}} ==Professional career== ===Miami Heat (2004–2010)=== Wright was selected 19th overall by the Heat in the [[2004 NBA draft]].{{cite web|last1=News-Times |first1=The (Danbury |url=http://www.newstimes.com/news/article/From-South-Kent-to-the-NBA-109907.php|title=From South Kent to the NBA|work=NewsTimes.com|date=March 2, 2005|access-date=April 12, 2016}} On February 5, 2005, he made his professional debut in a 108–97 win over the [[Chicago Bulls]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=250205014|title=Miami wins 5 of last 6|work=ESPN.com|date=February 5, 2005|access-date=April 12, 2016}}{{dead link|date=July 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}} On January 3, 2006, Wright was assigned to the [[Florida Flame]] of the [[NBA G League|NBA Development League]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/heat/news/wright_barron_fl_flame_60103.html|title=Dorell Wright & Earl Barron assigned to Florida Flame|date=January 3, 2006|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|access-date=January 3, 2006}} On January 18, he was recalled by the Heat.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/wright_barron_recalled.html|title=Heat Recall Barron and Wright From Florida|date=January 18, 2006|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|access-date=January 18, 2006|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151003162941/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/wright_barron_recalled.html|archive-date=October 3, 2015}} At the end of the year, he was the youngest member of the Heat's first NBA championship squad.{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/teams/MIA/2006.html|title=2005-06 Miami Heat Roster and Stats|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=April 13, 2016}} On August 21, 2008, Wright re-signed with the Heat.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3547583|title=Heat re-sign improving forward Wright|date=August 21, 2008|work=ESPN.com|access-date=August 21, 2008}} ===Golden State Warriors (2010–2012)=== [[File:Dorell Wright 030211.jpg|thumb|left|Wright with the Warriors in 2011]] On July 12, 2010, Wright signed with the [[Golden State Warriors]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors_sign_dorell_wright_071210.html|title=Warriors Sign Free Agent Forward Dorell Wright|date=July 12, 2010|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|access-date=July 12, 2010}} On November 27, he set a franchise record with nine three-point field goals made, surpassing [[Jason Richardson]]'s record of eight three-pointers set on March 29, 2007.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20101127/GSWMIN/gameinfo.html|title=Wright's 9 3s lift Warriors over Timberwolves|date=November 27, 2010|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|access-date=November 28, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101201131851/http://www.nba.com/games/20101127/GSWMIN/gameinfo.html|archive-date=December 1, 2010|url-status=dead}} On February 8, 2011, he was selected to compete in the 3-Point Shootout at the 2011 NBA All-Star Weekend in Los Angeles.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/dorell_wright_three_point_shootout.html|title=Dorell Wright To Compete In 2011 Foot Locker Three-Point Contest|work=NBA.com|date=February 8, 2011|access-date=February 8, 2011}} On March 18, 2011, against the [[Phoenix Suns]], Wright went scoreless in the first half, but scored 30 points in the second half in a 108–97 loss. He finished the game with 30 points, 6 rebounds, 2 assists, and 2 blocks.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20110318/GSWPHX/gameinfo.html|title=Warriors-Suns notebook|work=NBA.com|date=March 18, 2011|access-date=April 13, 2016}} On March 23, he scored a career-high 34 points to go with 5 rebounds and 6 assists against the [[Houston Rockets]] in a 131–112 loss.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20110323/GSWHOU/gameinfo.html|title=Warriors-Rockets notebook|work=NBA.com|date=March 23, 2011|access-date=March 24, 2011}} On April 6, 2011, Wright set a Warriors franchise record for three-point shots made in a season with 184 in a home win versus the [[Los Angeles Lakers]], beating [[Jason Richardson]]'s previous record of 183 in the 2005–06 season.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20110406/LALGSW/gameinfo.html|title=Warriors hand Lakers third straight loss, 95-87|work=NBA.com|date=April 6, 2011|access-date=April 13, 2016}} On April 13, 2011, he became the first player in NBA history to have scored more points in his seventh season than all of his first six combined in a win against the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20110413/PORGSW/gameinfo.html|title=Trail Blazers-Warriors|work=NBA.com|date=April 13, 2011|access-date=April 13, 2016}} He also ended the season with the most [[3-point field goal|three-point shots]] made in the [[2010–11 NBA season|2010–11 season]] with 194, as well as the most three-point field goals attempted with 516, both of which set Warriors franchise records.{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/w/wrighdo01/shooting/2011/|title=Dorell Wright 2010-11 Shooting|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=April 13, 2016}} The records were surpassed by [[Stephen Curry]] in the [[2012–13 NBA season|2012–13 season]], when Curry set the NBA record for three-point field goals made.{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/c/curryst01/shooting/2013/|title=Stephen Curry 2012-13 Shooting|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=April 13, 2016}} After the 2010–11 season, Wright finished third in voting for [[NBA Most Improved Player]], behind [[LaMarcus Aldridge]] and [[Kevin Love]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2011/news/04/21/love-most-improved/|title=Wolves' Love wins Kia Most Improved Player Award|work=NBA.com|date=April 21, 2011|access-date=April 12, 2016|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150918233038/http://www.nba.com/2011/news/04/21/love-most-improved/|archive-date=September 18, 2015}} {{clear}} ===Philadelphia 76ers (2012–2013)=== [[File:Dorell Wright 76ers.jpg|thumb|right|Wright with the 76ers in 2013]] On July 11, 2012, Wright was traded to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] in a three-team trade.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/8157582/golden-state-warriors-deal-dorell-wright-get-jarrett-jack-3-team-trade|title=Hornets join 76ers-Warriors swap|work=ESPN.com|date=July 11, 2012|access-date=July 11, 2012}} On October 31, 2012, he made his debut for the 76ers in an 84–75 win over to the [[Denver Nuggets]], recording three points, one rebound and one assist in 16 minutes.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20121031/DENPHI/gameinfo.html|title=Hawes' double-double lifts 76ers past Denver 84-75|work=NBA.com|date=October 31, 2012|access-date=April 12, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121029053920/http://www.nba.com/games/20121031/DENPHI/gameinfo.html|archive-date=October 29, 2012|url-status=dead}} ===Portland Trail Blazers (2013–2015)=== On July 10, 2013, Wright signed with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].{{cite web|url=http://www.iamatrailblazersfan.com/ArticleDisplay/tabid/297/ItemID/3865/Default.aspx |title=Trail Blazers Sign Dorell Wright |work=IAmATrailBlazersFan.com |date=July 10, 2013 |access-date=July 10, 2013 |url-status=usurped |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131112172841/http://www.iamatrailblazersfan.com/ArticleDisplay/tabid/297/ItemID/3865/Default.aspx |archive-date=November 12, 2013 }} On October 30, 2013, he made his debut for the Trail Blazers in a 104–91 loss to the [[Phoenix Suns]], recording three points, one rebound and one assist in 16 minutes.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20131030/PORPHX/gameinfo.html|title=Dragic, Bledsoe help Suns give Hornacek 1st win|work=NBA.com|date=October 30, 2013|access-date=April 12, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160330123654/http://www.nba.com/games/20131030/PORPHX/gameinfo.html|archive-date=March 30, 2016|url-status=dead}} ===Beikong Fly Dragons (2015–2016)=== On August 17, 2015, Wright signed with the [[Beikong Fly Dragons]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]].{{cite web|url=http://www.asia-basket.com/China/news/417430/Chongqing-Fly-Dragon-lands-Dorell-Wright|title=Chongqing Fly Dragon lands Dorell Wright|work=Asia-Basket.com|date=August 17, 2015|access-date=October 11, 2015}} In 37 games for the Dragons, he averaged 24.3 points, 7.5 rebounds, 2.5 assists and 2.0 steals per game. ===Return to the Heat (2016)=== On April 12, 2016, Wright signed with the [[Miami Heat]], returning to the franchise for a second stint.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/heat/heat-signs-dorell-wright|title=HEAT SIGNS DORELL WRIGHT|work=NBA.com|date=April 12, 2016|access-date=April 12, 2016}} On April 17, Wright checked in during the final minutes of a 123–91 win over the [[Charlotte Hornets]] in Game 1 of the first round of the playoffs. He received a standing ovation from what remained of the home crowd. In his first appearance for the Heat in six years, he scored eight points on 3-of-3 shooting.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160417/CHAMIA/gameinfo.html|title=Deng scores 31 points, Heat rout Hornets 123–91 in Game 1|work=NBA.com|date=April 17, 2016|access-date=April 20, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160417230131/http://www.nba.com/games/20160417/CHAMIA/gameinfo.html|archive-date=April 17, 2016|url-status=dead}} Wright's final NBA game was Game 7 of the 2016 Eastern Conference Semifinals on May 15, 2016, in a 89–116 loss to the [[Toronto Raptors]]. This was the only game of the series that Wright played in and he played for 2 and half minutes (substituting in at the very end of the 4th quarter for Goran Dragic). Wright recorded 2 points and 1 rebound. On September 26, 2016, Wright signed with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]],{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/clippers/news/training-camp-roster-2016|title=L.A. CLIPPERS ANNOUNCE TRAINING CAMP ROSTER|work=NBA.com|date=September 26, 2016|access-date=September 26, 2016}} but was waived on October 12 after appearing in two preseason games.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/clippers/news/clippers-waive-munford-and-wright|title=Clippers Waive Munford and Wright|work=NBA.com|date=October 12, 2016|access-date=October 12, 2016}} ===Europe (2017–2020)=== On October 3, 2017, Wright signed with [[KK Igokea|Igokea]] for the 2017–18 season.{{cite news|title=Igokea sign contract with NBA champion Dorell Wright|url=http://www.aba-liga.com/news.php?id=38781|access-date=October 3, 2017|work=aba-liga.com|date=October 3, 2017}} After only four games he left Igokea and on October 27, 2017, he signed with German club [[Brose Bamberg]] for the rest of the season.{{cite news|title=Dorell Wright verstärkt Brose Bamberg|url=https://www.brosebamberg.de/saison/news/nachricht/artikel/dorell-wright-verstaerkt-brose-bamberg/|access-date=October 27, 2017|work=brosebamberg.de|date=October 27, 2017|language=de}}{{cite news|title=Brose Bamberg announced the acquisition of Dorell Wright|url=http://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/541590/brose-bamberg-announced-acquisition-dorell-wright/|access-date=October 27, 2017|work=Eurohoops.net|date=October 27, 2017}} On July 20, 2018, Wright signed a one-year deal with [[PBC Lokomotiv Kuban|Lokomotiv Kuban]] of the [[VTB United League]].{{cite news |title=Lokomotiv tabs Wright at forward |url=http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/8vvnad74msovw3vq |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180720165540/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/8vvnad74msovw3vq |url-status=dead |archive-date=July 20, 2018 |access-date=July 20, 2018 |work=EuroCupBasketball.com |date=July 20, 2018}} === Retirement and later ventures === On November 18, 2020, Wright announced his retirement from professional basketball on his [[Instagram]] page, after a 16-year career in the NBA, China, and Europe.{{cite web |last1=Askounis |first1=Johnny |title=Dorell Wright calls it a day |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/nba-news/1130553/dorell-wright-calls-it-a-day/ |website=Eurohoops |access-date=December 1, 2020 |date=November 18, 2020}} As of 2020, Wright has worked as a studio analyst for [[NBC Sports Bay Area]] on pre-game and post-game coverage.{{cite web | url=https://www.nbcsports.com/bayarea/warriors/nbc-sports-bay-area-announces-new-warriors-giants-prepost-talent | title=NBCSBA announces new pre/Post talent for Warriors, Giants | date=November 23,
